 In ETF activity last Friday, one fund was buying and none were selling. iShares PHLX SOX Semiconductor Sector Index Fund ( SOXX ) added $973.8 million of stock against no sales, lifting 29 positions and trimming none, with gross traded value of $973.8 million against $42.97 billion in assets.

 The largest buy was Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), where SOXX added 185,502 shares worth $93.6 million, bringing the position to 9.25% of assets. NVIDIA ( NVDA ) drew $80.9 million across 395,471 shares for a 7.99% weight, Micron Technology ( MU ) added 91,074 shares worth $80.6 million at 7.96%, Broadcom ( AVGO ) gained 235,769 shares for $76.9 million at 7.59%, and Intel ( INTC ) rose 975,455 shares for $64.1 million at 6.34%. None of the buys were new positions and the fund exited nothing. 
 How does SOXX invest? 
 SOXX is an Equity Sector Information Tech fund holding 30 stocks, with 61.1% of assets in its 10 largest holdings and all of its classified stock in Technology. Its market-cap mix is 100.0% large cap, with no mid- or small-cap exposure, and it charges 0.33%. Top holdings are Advanced Micro Devices at 9.25%, NVIDIA at 7.99%, Micron Technology at 7.96%, Broadcom at 7.59% and Intel at 6.34%. The fund has a GF Score of 88, a P/E of 44.13, a P/B of 11.62, a dividend yield of 0.29% and a year-to-date return of 50.9%.
